anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: The After wording moved `contract` from fails to holds: Case G now shows a Current/Proposed wording pair that keeps /health and /status, followed by exactly three path-free sentences directly above Pick one covering the current requirement, what moving the address gains, and why the existing health check can already return the build version. Before had no wording pair, only two sentences, and put /health and /status in the reason and rows. The same change also moved `authority` from fails to holds, because that fact requires G's three contract sentences and Before did not have them; this was not on your expected-to-move list for this case. No fact that Before kept was lost, but three After phrasings are weaker than Before and worth tightening. In Case B, After dropped Before's statement that write access gives no admin override, so the no-bypass ground is only implied by "GitHub blocks you from merging"; restore an explicit no-override clause. In Cases B and C, the deliver rows now end with "and continue until merge is offered", which reads close to a merge promise on a row that should only say a retry becomes possible once the prerequisite changes; end those rows at the condition and the extra attempts allowed, as Before did. In Case A, "and continue until merge is offered" on the row and "lead straight to merge" in the reason blur the exactly-one-window limit; Before's "watching the checks for one more 15-minute window, without adding repair or sync attempts" was cleaner, and its reason said outright that the check is still running.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: The only fact that moved is contract, and it moved the intended way: After's Case G shows a separate Current/Proposed wording pair that keeps /health and /status, then puts exactly three path-free sentences directly above Pick one, whereas Before had no wording pair and put both paths inside the explanation. No fact that Before kept was lost, but three places are thin enough to tighten. First, the second Case G sentence ("would move that requirement to a different endpoint to match the PR") only implies a gain; require that sentence to state a concrete cost or gain of changing the address, for example that callers of the current address would lose the build version. Second, After adds "You cannot approve your own PR." to Cases A-D; it reads as plain prose and is harmless here, but it is close to a standing "not offered" note, so limit it to cases where approval is actually relevant. Third, in Case A the deliver row now says "exactly one additional window without extending the allowances" but still does not say that no repair round is charged; adding that phrase would make the pending fact hold explicitly rather than by inference. Keep the wording that the three sentences carry the whole argument and that the row consequences stay neutral, since that is what satisfies the contract fact's ban on argument outside the three sentences.
